question.:question/problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $p - q$?

$\{4p=24; p+5q=-29$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. 

Using the first equation, we can isolate $p$ by dividing both sides by $4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4p & =24 \\ p & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $p=6$ into the second equation and solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}p+5q & =-29 \\ (6)+5q & =-29 \\ 5q & =-35 \\ q & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p-q=6-(-7)=13.$

$$

If we now substitute $a=-8$ into $b=240-4a,$ we can then find the value of $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =240-4(-8) \\ b & =272\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-8,\,b=272.$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+y & =8 \\ y & =8+2x\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

If we now substitute $x=-\frac{29}{6}$ into $y=8+2x,$ we can then find the value of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =8+2(-\frac{29}{6}) \\ y & =-\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
